added.summary: `--stage day` shows an effect on a grey ground under an overcast day instead of the dusk, so what is lit (smoke, dust, debris, a mark on the ground) reads; the default stays the dusk, where what glows reads. An effect of decals alone (a bullet hole, a skid mark) is now measured, on a lit ground from above, so its sheet frames the mark, and a mark flat on the ground is looked down on instead of seen as a line from the side.

An effect that leaves a mark (a `decal`) has its six frames taken over the time it drew anything else and a quarter more, instead of over its whole length: the last frame shows the mark alone and the others what left it, where most of the sheet showed only the mark. The record's `frameSeconds` lists when each frame was taken.

fixed.summary: An effect with a `decal` is anchored on the `ground` whatever it draws below its origin (a glow about a circle on the floor), since the decal lands on the surface there. It was measured `centre` when a tenth of it lay below, and its shots raised it off the ground, so the decal showed nowhere.
A sheet (`<effect>.png`, `together.png`) is written at PNG's best compression: the same pixels in a fifth of the bytes or less (a 2880x1080 sheet of about 3 MB is 0.2 to 0.7 MB).
